trace.final_message:
The contact sheet function is in place and committed on a new branch, `contact-sheet`, which I created because `main` is the default branch. Nothing is pushed. All thirty tests pass (the twenty-six existing ones plus four new ones), and `make lint` is clean.

The function is `contact_rows(students)` in `rosterkit/contacts.py`. It sorts students by display name ("Last, First"), then returns one string per student with the name, section and email in aligned columns. The name and section columns are sized to the longest value in the list, so the emails line up without fixed widths. An empty list raises `ValueError`. A student whose email is missing or only whitespace raises `ValueError` with the display name and student id in the message.

Some choices I made that you may want to change. I used `ValueError` rather than adding a new error class, which matches how the reader reports bad rows. The rows have no header line, since you asked for rows only. I did not export the function from `rosterkit/__init__.py`, because the house rules forbid `from ... import` lines and the package's existing exports use them. Instead, I added an entry to `docs/api.txt` and a line under Unreleased in `CHANGES.txt`. The new module imports the models module with `import rosterkit.models as models`, which is the only import style the project rules allow.

# owner: platform
import unittest
import rosterkit.models as models
import rosterkit.contacts as contacts


def make_student(last_name, first_name, section, email=None):
    """Student with an id derived from the name, to keep tests short."""
    student_id = last_name.lower()
    return models.Student(
        student_id, last_name, first_name, section, email
    )


def sample_roster():
    """Three students, deliberately out of name order."""
    return [
        make_student("Varrow", "Ines", "A", "varrow@example.invalid"),
        make_student("Thistle", "Bram", "A", "thistle@example.invalid"),
        make_student("Quillon", "Sefa", "B", "quillon@example.invalid"),
    ]


class ContactRowTests(unittest.TestCase):
    def test_rows_are_sorted_and_aligned(self):
        rows = contacts.contact_rows(sample_roster())
        expected = [
            "Quillon, Sefa  B  quillon@example.invalid",
            "Thistle, Bram  A  thistle@example.invalid",
            "Varrow, Ines   A  varrow@example.invalid",
        ]
        self.assertTrue(rows == expected)

    def test_empty_list_raises(self):
        with self.assertRaises(ValueError):
            contacts.contact_rows([])

    def test_missing_email_names_the_student(self):
        roster = sample_roster() + [make_student("Okafor", "Lena", "B")]
        with self.assertRaises(ValueError) as caught:
            contacts.contact_rows(roster)
        self.assertTrue("Okafor, Lena" in str(caught.exception))

    def test_blank_email_counts_as_missing(self):
        roster = [make_student("Dunmore", "Ravi", "A", "   ")]
        with self.assertRaises(ValueError):
            contacts.contact_rows(roster)
